title: The Hidden Colors We Can't Name
hook: You can see ten million colors, but how many can you name?
script: You can see ten million colors, but how many can you name? The human eye can distinguish approximately ten million different colors. So why do we only have names for about a thousand? Most people experience trichromatic vision with three types of cones. A rare few women possess a fourth type of cone, making them tetrachromats. These individuals can see up to a hundred million colors, a staggering difference. Yet, even for most of us, the shades we perceive often lack names. You would need a surface the size of the entire United States to paint every color.
